candidates.claim: Default range setting may never reach the panel: panel reads host.settings.get/onDidChange, an API no other code in the repo uses; errors are swallowed, so the panel silently opens on 7d.
candidates.trigger: 1. User sets Default range to 30d in plugin settings (orca-plugin.json:88 declares it). 2. Panel mounts; firstLoad() calls readDefaultRange(). 3. If Orca's panel host has no settings object, host?.settings?.get?.() yields undefined; the then at src/panel/panel.js:624 ignores it (not 1d/7d/30d/90d/all). 4. state.defaultRange stays '7d'; firstLoad loads 7d. Same for onDidChange at panel.js:596. Tests pass only because mountPanel injects orca.settings (tests/panel.test.mjs:138), the same guessed shape.
candidates.wrong: Should: panel reads the saved value through the host API the worker uses (orca.host.call('settings.get'), src/worker.mjs:353) or a verified panel equivalent. Does: silent fallback to 7d, no log, no error state.
candidates.confidence: medium; settle by Orca panel host API docs or a live panel run with a saved defaultRange of 30d. Repo has no definition of host.settings (rg across panel, src, docs, scripts).
candidates.class: unverified host API shape, failure swallowed as default
candidates.sweep: Other host calls in panel: host.plugin.request (panel.js request), host.plugin.on (panel.js:885), host.on('theme') (panel.js:886), all used at baseline eae3fa0 -> checked-fine as existing shapes. Only host.settings.* is new (panel.js:596, 623). Worker uses orca.host.call('settings.get') (src/worker.mjs:353, 371) -> not-same shape, not-checked for panel.

candidates.claim: Slow Default range read: 1.5 s fallback loads 7d, then the setting moves state.range to 30d; the stale 7d response renders under the 30d button.
candidates.trigger: 1. Panel opens; host settings.get takes over 1500 ms. 2. Timer at panel.js:599 fires: state.report null, not busy, so load() sends usage.report range 7d. 3. Read answers '30d'; firstLoad (panel.js:603-606) sets state.range = '30d' and aria-checked on the 30d button. 4. The 7d request answers; load() (panel.js:47-80) calls render() without checking the range it asked for. 5. Panel shows 7d numbers with 30d selected; the queued second load (state.again, panel.js:50-53) then corrects it.
candidates.wrong: Should: no render of a report for a range that is no longer selected. Does: brief mismatched render, then corrected by a second load.
